_meta.title: Cooked Finance educational score methodology
_meta.scope: A deterministic educational estimate based only on the seven values a visitor enters. It is not a population percentile, credit score, financial plan, or prediction.
_meta.disclaimer: For educational purposes only. The score is a simplified starting point, not financial, investment, tax, or legal advice.
_meta.inputConsistency: Use one adult's personal figures for every field. Run a separate check for a partner; combining adults makes the age-based retirement guidepost misleading.
notIncluded: Taxes, government benefits, projected defined-benefit pension income, or employer matching not explicitly included in the monthly-saving input
Home equity, property, or other assets
Dependents, cost of living, retirement age, or risk tolerance
Any comparison with other people or households

sources.title: What is a debt-to-income ratio?
sources.supports: DTI is monthly debt payments divided by gross monthly income. The source does not define Cooked Finance score thresholds.

sources.title: Guide to emergency savings
sources.supports: A general goal of 3 to 6 months of essential expenses in emergency savings. Personal needs can differ.

sources.title: How much do I need to retire?
sources.supports: General retirement-savings guideposts of 1x income at 30, 3x at 40, 6x at 50, 8x at 60, and 10x at 67, plus a general 15% annual savings guideline including employer contributions. Personal targets can differ.

scoring.weightNote: Weights are Cooked Finance editorial choices. They sum to 1.00 and are not survey estimates or lender rules.

curves._note: Each curve is a transparent piecewise-linear Cooked Finance scale of [metric, pillar score]. Pillar scores run from 0 to 100. Anchors between externally sourced guideposts are editorial modeling choices, not population benchmarks.

retirementGuideposts.interpolation: For ages 30 through 67, Cooked Finance linearly interpolates between Fidelity's published guideposts. For ages above 67, the model holds the 10x guidepost constant.

earlyCareerModel.method: Ages 18 through 25 use a 0.1x modeling floor. Ages 26 through 29 linearly rise from 0.1x at 25 to Fidelity's published 1x at 30. The 0.1x floor is a Cooked Finance product assumption, not a Fidelity milestone.

retirementGuideposts.limitations: These guideposts assume retirement around 67 and other assumptions described by Fidelity. They are broad planning guideposts, not personalized targets.
